reviewer: Codex and sole fresh-context GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer

claims.summary: For q>=2, a categorical width-k CNF or DNF F on [q]^n, k>=1, under independent whole-coordinate p-live/uniform-fixed restrictions, the canonical term-query decision tree has Pr[height>=s]<=a^s for integer s>=1, a=2q^2*k*p/(1-p). The proof adapts the classical Beame/Razborov encoding with masks, actual q-ary path values and product-measure weights, including a partial last batch. If mu is the uniform full-cube mean of F, then Pr[F restricted is nonzero]<=q^t*mu+a^(t+1) for every integer t>=0. Bounds above one are vacuous; clause count does not enter. This is a proved categorical adaptation, not a claim of independent novelty.
claims.assessment: Working all-parameter categorical encoding and density argument, passed by the sole fresh medium reviewer; exhaustive small binary/ternary encoding controls passed. Classical mechanism adapted with explicit law and constants.
claims.rationale: Keeps the actual categorical restriction law and converts scalar error rarity into a sufficient probability of zero restricted error, without a false fixed-restriction rank inference.
claims.next_action: Use only with a justified error representation and coherent sampler; compare its required width with actual source errors.

claims.summary: For a finite complete acyclic binary ENS source over a q-label one-hot old domain, at most M>=1 companions and all original generator degrees<=B>=2, supply a distribution on coherent old polynomial coefficient maps of degree<=T>=1. Every companion function for every map in that distribution's support has categorical CNF width<=k>=1, and each has average uniform-label mean<=epsilon. An independent p-live uniform-label restriction preserves old PC hardness through T*B with probability>=1-eta. If eta+M*(q^t*epsilon+a^(t+1))<1 for some integer t>=0, a=2q^2*k*p/(1-p), the source has no degree-B PC/NS refutation. One map/restriction makes every error locally zero at original substituted degree; one-hot division and complete replay pay T*B. Uniform independent scalar rows give T=1,epsilon=2^(-h) and sufficient a<=q^(-2), eta+M*(2^(-h/2)+2^(-h))<1. For the fixed growing charged family Delta=n^alpha,p=n^-beta,0<beta<alpha and alpha*(ell-1)+beta<1, h=ceil(n^alpha log n),B=ceil(h^ell log n),q=3, k<=(1-p)/(162p) fit every fixed polynomial original inventory when that sampler width premise holds. A deterministic paired-row sampler on coordinate indicators instead has width2 and epsilon<=(5/9)^h, also fitting this family. No arbitrary mixed-source sampler is supplied.
claims.assessment: Working switching/first-moment/complete-source composition, including polynomial maps and a fixed-coordinate sampler repair; the sole medium reviewer passed the one-hot certificates, TB replay and original-encoding calibration. Requires a supplied sampler; no unrestricted coverage.
claims.rationale: Uses a supplied joint map distribution rather than requiring all scalar choices or source errors to be independent; preserves original degree and a common hard restriction.
claims.next_action: Carry the still-missing low-width sampler for arbitrary mixtures to the scheduled route review; uniform sampling fails the companion width control.

claims.summary: For m>=32 and 1<=h<=m/16, uniform C in F2^(h by m), and distinguished-label indicators z_i on m distinct coordinates of a q>=2 label cube, E_C=z_1 product_(u<=h)(1+(Cz)_u) has old degree<=h+1. With probability>=1-(2^h-1)exp(-m/16), rank C=h, e_1 is not in its row space, and every categorical CNF for E_C has a clause of width>=ceil(m/4)-1. Every nonzero row combination has weight>=m/4 on this event; projecting the support Cz=0,z_1=1 onto smaller sets gives only the z_1 constraint. If these indicators form a free old cube in proper J_D, a nonzero row L supplies a surviving degree-one weight killing all companions through h+2; complete replay fits 1+max(u,2h+1)<=D. This refutes automatic narrow width for uniform scalar sampling, not optimized removal. For the same coordinate tuple, deterministic disjoint paired rows have width-two categorical errors and ternary mean<=(5/9)^h, so a different sampler can bypass the width obstruction.
claims.assessment: Working all-parameter dual-code projection and weight/paired-sampler controls; the sole medium reviewer passed probability, width, proper-quotient embedding and both repair scopes.
claims.rationale: Separates actual error CNF width from low polynomial degree and weighted removability, and tests the failed uniform policy against a concrete alternative on the same source.
claims.next_action: Do not require every sampler to be narrow; seek an appropriate source-dependent sampler or retain actual weighted-error methods for noncoordinate mixtures.

claims.summary: Let V<=F2^m have dimension r>h>=1 and minimum nonzero weight>=d>=1. Use a basis of V as linear-form inputs on distinguished-label indicators of m distinct q>=2 coordinates. For every h-row binary scalar coefficient assignment, some nonzero companion has categorical CNF width>=d: choose an input outside the selected row space, whose proper nonempty affine support has every projection to fewer than d coordinates full. Thus no scalar-map distribution can meet an all-errors width<d premise. For m>=64,h<=floor(m/64), codes with r=floor(m/32),d=ceil(m/4) exist by the explicit random-generator union bound. If the indicator coordinates lie in a free old cube, selecting g1 as one row and W=g1 gives a surviving degree-one weight killing all companions through degree3, with original replay 1+B<=D, B>=max(u,2h+1). The obstruction concerns unweighted pre-restriction scalar maps, not polynomial coefficients, restriction-dependent choices or weighted removal.
claims.assessment: Working author-verified extension suggested and then passed by the same medium reviewer on follow-up; affine projection, unbounded code existence and degree-three weight repair are supplied in full. Limits scalar pre-restriction width, not weighted or polynomial-map removal.
claims.rationale: Tests whether changing the scalar sampler can always repair the uniform-width failure, and shows a different noncoordinate source class where it cannot while weighted removal remains cheap.
claims.next_action: Use this scope limit in the scheduled architecture review; retain polynomial-map and weighted-error alternatives rather than treating narrow scalar errors as necessary.

Its fixed-family application uses the hard live-graph event and original canonical charge encoding, not the separate signed-mass estimate.
Pays original encoding length and fixed depth-dependent graph parameters independent of the polynomial inventory exponent.
Uses its paired ternary probability calculation for a fixed sampler and distinguishes restriction averaging from fixed-domain rank.
Embeds the wide-error control in a proper old quotient and certifies survival of its degree-one row weight.
The deterministic paired-row repair uses the recorded narrow error functions, retaining outside coordinate companions.
Different consequence of restriction: decision-tree depth and rare-function survival rather than literal subclause pruning.
Its uniform-sampling width failure is explicitly a limitation of that particular sampler; the theorem permits other supplied distributions.
Uses the same projection/width and random-generator counting mechanisms for a fixed high-distance input space against every scalar choice.
Certifies survival of the linear weight in the actual proper old quotient; the width claim itself is a full-label-space statement.
Limits the pre-restriction narrow-width premise for scalar samplers on this code family, leaving the theorem's polynomial-map option and weighted alternatives open.
